name: ScanSource, Inc.
reason: Low-margin specialty IT distributor (EBIT margin 3.2%, 10y ROIC 5.1%) with revenue shrinking 0.9%/yr over 10y and EPS at 1.0x its 10y high; a cheap but ordinary middleman with no moat or secular driver.

name: Patrick Industries, Inc.
reason: Component supplier to cyclical RV/marine/MH OEMs whose growth was acquisition-led (acquisitions 1.22x 10y FCF) with net debt/EBITDA 3.3x and EPS that halved in 2023 (-52%); earnings track RV shipments, which cannot be forecast.

name: Avista Corporation
reason: Regulated Pacific Northwest utility with 1.9%/yr 10y EPS growth, shares rising 2.6%/yr, negative FCF and net debt/EBITDA 5.1x; no route to >=7% EPS growth and wildfire-liability exposure.

name: NCR Voyix Corporation
reason: Post-breakup retail/restaurant tech business with revenue down 8.3%/yr over 10y, GAAP losses in 2023-24 (adjusted-GAAP gap 262%) and 10y ROIC of 1%; a shrinking, restructuring business with no visible specialness.

name: Papa John's International, Inc.
reason: Pizza franchisor with EPS at 0.41x its 10y high, 10y EPS CAGR -3.7%, net debt/EBITDA 4.8x and negative equity from buybacks (1.49x FCF); share loss to Domino's and aggregators leaves no credible growth route.

name: Winnebago Industries, Inc.
reason: Highly cyclical RV/marine maker with EPS collapsing from 13.81 (2022) to 1.67 (0.12x peak), EBIT margin 2.0% and net debt/EBITDA 3.6x after acquisitions; earnings set by discretionary RV demand and rates.

name: Baxter International Inc.
reason: Levered Hillrom acquisition left net debt/EBITDA 4.7x, EBIT margin 6.2% vs 16.8% peak, adjusted EPS 0.61x its 10y high and negative consensus LTG (-3.2%); acquisition-driven, deteriorating franchise with product-quality issues.

name: Halliburton Company
reason: Oilfield services earnings are set by upstream capex and oil prices (EPS -0.02 in 2016, 0.65 in 2020, 3.13 in 2023) with 10y ROIC of 1.5%; commodity-driven and unforecastable.

name: Clorox Company
reason: Strong brands but adjusted EPS grew only 1.2%/yr over 10y (FY26 5.53 vs 7.72 in FY25), net debt/EBITDA 4.8x, private-label and ERP disruption; good business with no route to >=7% EPS growth.

name: PG&E Corporation
reason: Wildfire-liability utility that went bankrupt in 2019, with shares up 16.3%/yr over 10y from equity dilution, net debt/EBITDA 6.1x and EPS 0.38x its 2018 level; regulatory and litigation risk make it unforecastable and the balance sheet fails.

name: Fluor Corporation
reason: Fixed-price EPC contractor with a 10y average EBIT margin of 1.3%, a -10.87 EPS loss in 2019, negative 2025 operating margin and net debt/EBITDA 10.9x; project-execution and NuScale stake outcomes cannot be forecast.

name: Fifth Third Bancorp
reason: Solid Midwest/Southeast regional bank (10y ROE 11.8%, shares -1.8%/yr) but EPS is 0.95x its 10y high on a rate tailwind and the pending Comerica merger transforms the balance sheet, so the combined franchise cannot be forecast with confidence yet.

name: Kemper Corp
reason: Non-standard auto insurer with three straight loss years (2021-23 EPS -3.40/-2.46/-0.74), 10y ROE 3.3% and FY1 consensus EPS -44%; volatile, poorly underwritten specialty auto book fails the disciplined-underwriter test.

name: Lincoln National Corp
reason: Spread- and market-sensitive life/annuity insurer with a -5.22 EPS loss in 2022, capital strain that forced the Fortitude Re reinsurance deal and Bain preferred, and 10y ROE 7%; earnings driven by rates, equity markets and opaque reserve assumptions.

name: Bank of America Corp
reason: Buffett-held, low-cost-deposit universal bank with no acquisitions in 10y, shares down 3.7%/yr, adjusted EPS compounding 11.3%/yr (worst year 2020 -32%) and consensus LTG ~16%; main caveat is EPS at 1.0x its 10y high on a rate tailwind and Global Markets volatility.

name: MAXIMUS, Inc.
reason: Record is strong (EPS 11.9%/yr over 10y, 8/10 years >=7%, net debt/EBITDA 1.7x) but EPS is 1.0x its 10y high and almost all revenue comes from government contracts exposed to federal spending cuts, Medicaid policy and rebids; a 7.3x P/E reflects that risk.

name: Scotts Miracle-Gro Company
reason: The Hawthorne cannabis bust crushed EPS from 9.23 (2021) to 1.21 (2023), it remains 0.41x the 10y peak with net debt/EBITDA 3.9x, and lawn and garden demand is weather-driven and flat (10y revenue +1.2%/yr).

name: American Eagle Outfitters, Inc.
reason: Teen apparel retailer exposed to fashion risk with a 10y EPS CAGR of 3.2%, a loss in 2020 and EBIT margin 6.0% vs a 12.1% peak; cheap but ordinary, with no durable moat.

name: Dick's Sporting Goods, Inc.
reason: Best-in-class sporting goods retailer (EPS 16.5%/yr over 10y, shares -3.1%/yr, 10y ROIC 15.5%) but the 2025 Foot Locker acquisition cut EBIT margin to 7.7%, lifted net debt/EBITDA to 3.5x and cut consensus LTG to 1.5%, so the combined business cannot yet be forecast.

name: Avnet, Inc.
reason: Semiconductor-cycle-driven component distributor with EBIT margin of about 3%, 10y ROIC of 4.5%, FCF of only 0.08x net income over 10y (working-capital swings) and net debt/EBITDA 3.3x; EPS swings with the chip cycle (8.06 in 2023 to 3.44 in 2025).
